lines.text: Have you ever wondered why the sky keeps changing?
Let's watch the Sun, the Earth and the Moon move together!
The Earth is always spinning, like a spinning top.
The Sun shines on one half of it.
When your home faces the Sun, it's daytime.
When your home turns away from the Sun, it's nighttime.
One whole spin takes one day.
A long time ago, people cut each day into twenty four pieces.
We call those pieces hours.
The Moon travels around the Earth.
The Moon has no light of its own. The Sun lights up half of it, like a lamp shining on a ball.
As the Moon goes around, we see more or less of its bright side.
That's why the Moon seems to change its shape!
One trip around the Earth takes about one month.
The Moon changes to a new shape about every seven days.
So people made a week. Seven days!
The Earth also travels all the way around the Sun.
One whole trip takes one year.
The Earth is a little bit tilted.
When your side leans toward the Sun, you get more sunshine. That's summer.
When your side leans away, you get less. That's winter.
Sometimes, the Moon passes exactly between the Sun and the Earth.
It blocks the sunlight, and its shadow falls on the Earth.
The sky gets dark in the middle of the day! That's a solar eclipse.
It doesn't happen every month, because the Moon usually passes a little above or below the Sun.
And remember: never look straight at the Sun!
One spin of the Earth is a day.
One trip of the Moon is a month.
One trip around the Sun is a year.
Isn't the sky amazing?
